/-!
# Guy's conjecture on the crossing number of complete graphs

A *drawing* of a graph in the plane maps the vertices to distinct points and every edge to a
simple arc (an arbitrary curve, not necessarily a straight line segment) joining the images of
its endpoints, so that no vertex lies on an edge that it is not an endpoint of, and any two edges
meet in finitely many points outside their endpoints. A *crossing* is such a common point, counted
once for every pair of edges passing through it. The crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G)$ of $G$ is
the minimum number of crossings over all drawings of $G$.

Guy (1960) exhibited drawings of the complete graph $K_n$ showing that
$$\mathrm{cr}(K_n) \le Z(n) := \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor
\left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor
\left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor,$$
and conjectured that no drawing of any complete graph does better, i.e. $\mathrm{cr}(K_n) = Z(n)$
for all $n$. This is known for $n \le 12$ (Saaty, Pan–Richter) and open in general.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gu60] Guy, R. K., *A combinatorial problem*, Nabla (Bull. Malayan Math. Soc.) 7 (1960), 68–72.
- [PaRi07] Pan, S. and Richter, R. B., *The crossing number of $K_{11}$ is 100*,
  J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 128–134.
-/

blocks.docstring:
A (topological) drawing of the simple graph `G` in the plane. Vertices are mapped to distinct
points, and every edge is mapped to a simple arc (an injective continuous curve) whose two
endpoints are the images of the endpoints of the edge. The interior of an arc passes through no
vertex, and any two distinct arcs have only finitely many common interior points. Edges are
allowed to be arbitrary curves, not just straight line segments.

The arcs are not required to cross transversally at their common interior points: every common
interior point of two arcs is counted as a crossing. Since a touching point can be removed by a
local redrawing without creating new crossings, this does not change the minimum number of
crossings.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `Path`/`ContinuousMap` (used for the arcs; `Path` alone was unsuitable because edges are unordered), `IsEmbedding` for Jordan curves as in Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean, `UnitDistancePlaneGraph` (a geometric graph, not a drawing). Mathlib has no planar-graph or graph-embedding notion (only a TODO mention in SimpleGraph/Coloring.lean).
justification.name: CrossingNumber2.Drawing
justification.why_needed: No notion of a (topological) plane drawing of a graph exists in Mathlib or the repo. Fields: injective vertex placement `V → ℝ²`; for each edge `e : G.edgeSet` an injective continuous curve `C(I, ℝ²)` (simple arc) whose unordered endpoint pair equals `Sym2.map vertex e`; arc interiors (`Set.Ioo 0 1` in `I`) avoid every vertex point; any two distinct arcs have finitely many common interior points. This matches the Wikipedia definition (curves allowed, not rectilinear).

noncomputable def Drawing.crossings (D : Drawing G) : ℕ∞ :=
  {x : ℝ² × Sym2 G.edgeSet | ∃ e f, e ≠ f ∧ x.2 = s(e, f) ∧
    x.1 ∈ D.arc e '' Set.Ioo 0 1 ∩ D.arc f '' Set.Ioo 0 1}.encard
blocks.docstring:
The number of crossings of a drawing: the number of pairs `(p, {e, f})` where `e ≠ f` are
edges and `p` is a common point of the arcs of `e` and `f` other than a shared endpoint
(equivalently, a common interior point of the two arcs). A point through which several edges pass
is thus counted once for every pair of edges through it. The count is finite whenever `G` has
finitely many edges.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.ncard / Nat.card (rejected in favour of encard for honesty on infinite graphs); a Finset sum over Sym2 pairs (needs Fintype/Decidable instances, less generic).
justification.name: CrossingNumber2.Drawing.crossings
justification.why_needed: The number of crossings of a drawing: `Set.encard` of `{(p, {e,f}) | e ≠ f, p a common interior point of arc e and arc f}` in `ℝ² × Sym2 G.edgeSet`. This counts a crossing point once per unordered pair of edges through it, exactly as Wikipedia specifies. Valued in ℕ∞ (finite for finite graphs) to avoid the `ncard`-of-infinite-set-is-0 artefact.

blocks.docstring:
Guy's upper bound
$Z(n) = \frac14 \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-1)/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor
\lfloor (n-3)/2 \rfloor$
on the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$. The product is always divisible by `4`, so the
natural number division is exact.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib; the analogous Zarankiewicz bound is also absent from the repo.
justification.name: CrossingNumber2.guyBound
justification.why_needed: Guy's bound Z(n) = ¼⌊n/2⌋⌊(n-1)/2⌋⌊(n-2)/2⌋⌊(n-3)/2⌋ as a ℕ-valued function using truncated subtraction/division; the product is always divisible by 4 so division is exact (values for n = 5..14 and vanishing for n ≤ 4 are verified by `decide`/`rfl` test theorems).

blocks.name: guyBound
blocks.text:
/-- Guy's upper bound
$Z(n) = \frac14 \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-1)/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor
\lfloor (n-3)/2 \rfloor$
on the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$. The product is always divisible by `4`, so the
natural number division is exact. -/
def guyBound (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  n / 2 * ((n - 1) / 2) * ((n - 2) / 2) * ((n - 3) / 2) / 4

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question whose conjectured answer is 'No': for every n, every (topological, curves allowed, not rectilinear) drawing of K_n has at least Z(n) = (1/4)⌊n/2⌋⌊(n-1)/2⌋⌊(n-2)/2⌋⌊(n-3)/2⌋ crossings, i.e. cr(K_n) = Z(n) (the ≤ direction being Guy's known upper bound); 'any complete graph' is an existential over n, so answer(False) to the existence question is equivalent to the universal lower bound, Z(n) is an integer for all n (and 0 for n ≤ 4, where K_n is planar), and no crossing-number definitions exist yet in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
claims.reviewer_why: c01 states the list-entry question literally: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n, ∃ D : Drawing (completeGraph (Fin n)), D.crossings < guyBound n`, so answer(False) is exactly the universal lower bound cr(K_n) ≥ Z(n). Its bespoke `Drawing` is a clean topological (curved, non-rectilinear) model: injective vertex map into ℝ², each edge an injective continuous curve with the right endpoints, interiors avoiding all vertices, finitely many pairwise common interior points; `crossings` counts (point, unordered edge pair) with e ≠ f via `encard`, so shared endpoints are excluded and a k-fold point counts C(k,2) times, matching Wikipedia's counting convention. `guyBound` uses exact ℕ floor division (product divisible by 4, tests check the values 1,3,...,315 and 0 for n ≤ 4). Dropping transversality (touchings counted as crossings) does not change the minimum, since any such drawing can be redrawn as a proper polygonal drawing with no more crossings and every proper drawing is included with the same count. I only added a sentence to the `Drawing` docstring documenting this modeling choice. File compiles with only the `sorry` warning.

context:
In graph theory, the crossing number cr(G) of a graph G is the lowest number of edge crossings of a plane drawing of the graph G. For instance, a graph is planar if and only if its crossing number is zero. Determining the crossing number continues to be of great importance in graph drawing, as user studies have shown that drawing graphs with few crossings makes it easier for people to understand the drawing.
The study of crossing numbers originated in Turán's brick factory problem, in which Pál Turán asked for a factory plan that minimized the number of crossings between tracks connecting brick kilns to storage sites. Mathematically, this problem can be formalized as asking for the crossing number of a complete bipartite graph. The same problem arose independently in sociology at approximately the same time, in connection with the construction of sociograms. Turán's conjectured formula for the crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs remains unproven, as does an analogous formula for the complete graphs.
The crossing number inequality states that, for graphs where the number e of edges is sufficiently larger than the number n of vertices, the crossing number is at least proportional to e3/n2. It has applications in VLSI design and incidence geometry.
Without further qualification, the crossing number allows drawings in which the edges may be represented by arbitrary curves. A variation of this concept, the rectilinear crossing number, requires all edges to be straight li

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's reading (single yes/no question, conjectured answer 'No', topological drawings, Z(n) as stated, existential over n) is the one formalized.

/-!
# Guy's conjecture on the crossing number of complete graphs

$$\mathrm{cr}(K_n) \le Z(n) := \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor
\left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor
\left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor,$$
and conjectured that no drawing of any complete graph does better, i.e. $\mathrm{cr}(K_n) = Z(n)$
for all $n$. This is known for $n \le 12$ (Saaty, Pan–Richter) and open in general.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gu60] Guy, R. K., *A combinatorial problem*, Nabla (Bull. Malayan Math. Soc.) 7 (1960), 68–72.
- [PaRi07] Pan, S. and Richter, R. B., *The crossing number of $K_{11}$ is 100*,
  J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 128–134.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval

namespace CrossingNumber2

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- A (topological) drawing of the simple graph `G` in the plane. Vertices are mapped to distinct
points, and every edge is mapped to a simple arc (an injective continuous curve) whose two
endpoints are the images of the endpoints of the edge. The interior of an arc passes through no
vertex, and any two distinct arcs have only finitely many common interior points. Edges are
allowed to be arbitrary curves, not just straight line segments.

The arcs are not required to cross transversally at their common interior points: every common
interior point of two arcs is counted as a crossing. Since a touching point can be removed by a
local redrawing without creating new crossings, this does not change the minimum number of
crossings. -/
structure Drawing where
  /-- The position of each vertex in the plane. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The curve representing each edge, parametrised by the unit interval. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → C(I, ℝ²)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  arc_endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = Sym2.map vertex e
  arc_avoids_vertex (e : G.edgeSet) (t : I) (ht : t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) (v : V) : arc e t ≠ vertex v
  finite_inter (e f : G.edgeSet) (hef : e ≠ f) :
    (arc e '' Set.Ioo 0 1 ∩ arc f '' Set.Ioo 0 1).Finite

variable {G}

/-- The number of crossings of a drawing: the number of pairs `(p, {e, f})` where `e ≠ f` are
edges and `p` is a common point of the arcs of `e` and `f` other than a shared endpoint
(equivalently, a common interior point of the two arcs). A point through which several edges pass
is thus counted once for every pair of edges through it. The count is finite whenever `G` has
finitely many edges. -/
noncomputable def Drawing.crossings (D : Drawing G) : ℕ∞ :=
  {x : ℝ² × Sym2 G.edgeSet | ∃ e f, e ≠ f ∧ x.2 = s(e, f) ∧
    x.1 ∈ D.arc e '' Set.Ioo 0 1 ∩ D.arc f '' Set.Ioo 0 1}.encard

/-- Guy's upper bound
$Z(n) = \frac14 \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-1)/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor
\lfloor (n-3)/2 \rfloor$
on the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$. The product is always divisible by `4`, so the
natural number division is exact. -/
def guyBound (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  n / 2 * ((n - 1) / 2) * ((n - 2) / 2) * ((n - 3) / 2) / 4

/-- Guy's bound takes the values $1, 3, 9, 18, 36, 60, 100, 150, 225, 315$ for $n = 5, \dots, 14$
(OEIS A000241). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem guyBound_values :
    (List.range 10).map (fun i => guyBound (i + 5)) =
      [1, 3, 9, 18, 36, 60, 100, 150, 225, 315] := by
  decide

/-- Guy's bound vanishes for $n \le 4$, where $K_n$ is planar. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem guyBound_eq_zero (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 4) : guyBound n = 0 := by
  interval_cases n <;> rfl

/-- **Guy's conjecture on the crossing number of complete graphs.**
Is there a drawing of some complete graph $K_n$ with fewer than
$Z(n) = \frac14 \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-1)/2 \rfloor \lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor
\lfloor (n-3)/2 \rfloor$ crossings, the number given by Guy's upper bound? Guy conjectured that
the answer is no, i.e. that $\mathrm{cr}(K_n) = Z(n)$ for every $n$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem crossing_number_2 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ n, ∃ D : Drawing (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)), D.crossings < guyBound n := by
  sorry

end CrossingNumber2

items: The list-page entry is a yes/no question, so the statement is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n, ∃ D : Drawing (K_n), D.crossings < guyBound n` rather than an infimum-based `crossingNumber (K_n) = Z(n)`; per the decomposition notes, answer(False) ≡ ∀ n, every drawing of K_n has ≥ Z(n) crossings ≡ cr(K_n) = Z(n) given Guy's known upper bound. No `crossingNumber` (sInf) definition was introduced, avoiding sInf/empty-set subtleties.

Transversality ('proper crossings') is NOT required in `Drawing`: every common interior point of two arcs is counted, including touching points. Defining transversality for merely continuous curves is delicate, and the omission does not change the conjecture: a touching can be removed by a local redrawing without adding crossings (standard, e.g. Schaefer, Crossing Numbers of Graphs; Pach–Tóth), so a drawing with < Z(n) counted points exists iff a proper drawing with < Z(n) crossings exists. Reviewers should confirm they accept this.

Arcs are required to be injective (simple/Jordan arcs), the standard convention; Wikipedia's text says only 'curves', but self-intersections of a single edge are not counted as crossings and can be shortcut without adding crossings, so the minimum is unaffected.

Crossings between adjacent edges (sharing an endpoint) and multiple crossings of the same edge pair are counted, and a point on k edges counts C(k,2) times — exactly Wikipedia's counting convention ('counted separately for each crossing point, for each pair of edges'); crossing-minimal drawings never have these anyway.

The condition 'no vertex lies on an edge it is not an endpoint of' is encoded as: the open-interval part of every arc avoids all vertex points. Because arcs are injective with endpoints at the edge's vertices and vertex placement is injective, this is equivalent to the Wikipedia condition.

Finiteness of pairwise common interior points is a field of `Drawing` (as in Wikipedia's definition); `crossings` is ℕ∞-valued via `Set.encard`, and `D.crossings < guyBound n` compares in ℕ∞ with the automatic ℕ → ℕ∞ coercion.

Z(n) uses ℕ truncated subtraction and floor division; for n ≤ 3 the truncation gives 0 which agrees with the intended value (K_n planar for n ≤ 4). Verified values 1,3,9,18,36,60,100,150,225,315 for n = 5..14 (OEIS A000241) by `decide`.
K_n is `SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)` with n ranging over all ℕ (including n ≤ 4, where Z(n) = 0 makes the existential trivially false, matching the intended meaning).

AMS tag 5 (Combinatorics; 05C10 planar graphs). The generic `Drawing`/`crossings` definitions were kept in the problem file because the task permits writing only one file; a maintainer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

reviewer_notes: Verdicts on other candidates: c02 is fatally wrong — its crossing set requires `x.1.1 < x.1.2` on `{e : Finset (Fin n) // e.card = 2}`, where `<` is strict subset and never holds between 2-element finsets (verified in Lean), so crossingCount ≡ 0 and the statement becomes trivially `answer(True)`. c04 uses `answer(False)` for an open problem (repo convention is `answer(sorry)`) and adds an extra Mathlib import; otherwise its model is fine. c03, c05, c07 use equivalent relaxed set-based arc models and are faithful alternatives (c07 omits the finiteness axiom, relying on encard = ⊤; c05 uses ℕ-valued sums with ncard guarded by a finiteness axiom); they also add crossingNumber/eq/upper-bound variants which I did not ship to keep the file to exactly the adjudicated slot. c06 and c08 use a C¹ general-position model with fderiv-based transversality; this is also a standard equivalent model but considerably heavier, so c01 was preferred. Ambiguity in the source: 'any complete graph' read existentially over n : ℕ (n ≤ 4 gives Z(n) = 0 and cannot witness the existential), as in the decomposition notes. The only modeling caveat is the standard folklore equivalence that counting non-transverse touchings as crossings does not change the crossing number.
